name: Azure SQL Database
tagline: Microsoft's always-current managed SQL Server engine, from free serverless databases to 128 TB Hyperscale.
description: Azure SQL Database is Microsoft's platform-as-a-service flavor of the SQL Server engine, running the latest engine build ahead of boxed SQL Server releases. It offers provisioned and serverless compute (with auto-pause), elastic pools for multi-tenant SaaS, and the Hyperscale tier, which separates compute from a page-server storage layer to reach roughly 128 TB with fast backups and named read replicas. Recent additions include a native vector type and JSON type, ledger tables and Fabric mirroring. It is the natural home for .NET and T-SQL estates moving to the cloud; teams that need instance-level features such as SQL Agent or cross-database queries should look at Azure SQL Managed Instance instead.

pricing.notes: Free offer gives up to 10 serverless General Purpose databases with 100,000 vCore-seconds and 32 GB each per month; paid tiers by vCore or DTU, with reserved capacity and Azure Hybrid Benefit.

scale.notes: Hyperscale reaches ~128 TB with up to 30 named replicas; active geo-replication and failover groups provide readable cross-region secondaries; sharding via Elastic Database tools.

strengths: Always runs the newest SQL Server engine features, including native VECTOR and JSON types
Serverless tier auto-scales and auto-pauses; permanent free offer for small databases
Hyperscale separates compute and storage for ~128 TB databases with near-instant backups
Columnstore indexes, in-memory OLTP and temporal tables built in
Deep integration with Entra ID, Fabric mirroring and Defender
weaknesses: Azure-only and tied to T-SQL; porting away is costly
Lacks instance-level features (SQL Agent, cross-database queries, CLR) that Managed Instance offers
DTU/vCore/tier matrix makes cost planning confusing
useCases: .NET SaaS backends with elastic pools per tenant
Intermittent dev/test workloads on serverless auto-pause
Vector search alongside relational data for copilots
